title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-edgecase-debug-scratchpad-21
content:
Goal:
- Collect reproduction steps / commands tried / logs for the weird crash we see when cached_prefix_len + new_tokens crosses 2048 -> 4096 boundary.

Summary / Symptoms:
- Intermittent crash on long-prefix inference when model switches attention kernel. Mostly seen on rtx-a5000 clusters running cu113 + cutlass kernels.
- Failure only occurs when cached_tokens + request_tokens > 2048 (observed at 2049-4096 window). Works fine for <=2048 and also for >4096 in some runs (weird).
- Error messages observed (examples below) include CUDA kernel launch failures and OOB reads from attention kernel.

Key error snippets (copied from logs):
- runtime log: [2024-09-20 11:12:03] Error: CUDA kernel launch failed: invalid configuration argument
- stacktrace: RuntimeError: index out of bounds for dimension 1 at aten::index -> aten/src/.. (attention.cpp:432)
- device dump: attention_kernel_select: chosen_kernel=small_qk (max_seq=2048) predicted_total=3072 actual_total=3072
- nvsegfault: invalid read at 0x7f8c... (likely out-of-range kv read)

Hypothesis 1 (most likely): kernel selection uses an integer-truncated estimate derived from cached_prefix_len rounding down to chunk boundaries. When rounding logic is wrong, selected kernel reports max_seq=2048 but internal indexing expects up to 3072 (mismatch between kernel capability tag and actual implementation), so kernel tries to read KV positions beyond allocated chunk for its internal tileing -> OOB.
- Evidence: logs show selected_kernel=small_qk but kernel metadata passed in indicates tile size for 3k total tokens.
- Counter-evidence: Some runs with same inputs succeed (non-deterministic?). Maybe depends on allocator/placement pattern (address layout masks the OOB).

Hypothesis 2: cache eviction / kv cache pointer arithmetic bug when caching across kernel boundary. When we switch kernel variant mid-request (e.g., during continuous inference with caching across calls), the code path that migrates or rebinds KV pointers misses updating strides, leading to mis-indexing.

Commands / experiments tried so far (ordered):
1) Repro script minimal: python tests/repro/repro_seqlen_transition.py --model gpt-medium --prefix-len 2048 --new-tokens 1024 --device a5000
   - reproduces ~90% locally in docker:serving-runtime:canary
2) Run under cuda-memcheck: cuda-memcheck python ... -> shows invalid read at the same kernel symbol.
3) Insert ASSERT in attention kernel selector: assert(total_seq_len <= kernel.max_seq_len) -> assertion *does* fail for repro runs (so selection mismatch confirmed).
4) Force kernel selection to 'large_qk' (bypass selector) via env VAR ATTN_FORCE_KERNEL=large_qk -> reproducer no longer crashes (best evidence that small kernel path is broken).
5) Tried set ATTN_ROUNDING=ceil vs floor -> behavior changes, some runs succeed, some fail (rounding affects boundary but not full fix).
6) Added extra zero padding to KV buffer allocation (allocate +1 chunk) -> repro stops failing in many runs (suggests OOB read into adjacent allocated region previously).
7) Ran heavy randomized fuzzer (tests/fuzz/kv_cache_fuzzer) for 2 hours with seed 42 -> found 3 more failing cases with different sequence lengths (near other power-of-two-ish boundaries).

Quick diffs/places to inspect:
- serving-runtime/src/attention/kernel_selector.cpp: line ~218 (selection rounding and metadata composition)
- serving-runtime/src/kv_cache/kv_buffer.cpp: pointer arithmetic when append_cache_across_kernel_transition
- cutlass integration layer: serving-runtime/third_party/cutlass/wrappers/launch_params.h -> tile size / max seq metadata

Reproduction steps (clean):
- ./scripts/start_dev_container.sh (use image: serving-runtime:canary)
- python -m venv .venv; source .venv/bin/activate; pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
- pytest tests/repro/test_repl_seqlen_transition.py::test_repro_2048_to_3072 -q
- OR run single script: python tests/repro/repro_seqlen_transition.py --trace 1

Quick patch tried locally (hack):
- in kernel_selector.cpp, temporarily change rounding to always pick kernel with max_seq_len >= total_seq_len (i.e., ceil). This removed the assertion failures and the crash for the repro.
- downside: performance regression on some short-seq workloads; passing to bench team showed ~5-12% token throughput drop for typical short prompts.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Is the kernel metadata (max_seq_len) coming from compile-time constants in the cutlass library, or from runtime-queried kernel properties? If compile-time, maybe mismatch between build config and runtime assumption (we ship multiple builds?).
- Could allocator reuse pattern make OOB invisible sometimes? Yes. Need deterministic memory sanitizer (ASAN on CUDA isn't straightforward) but can run with O3 sanitizer on CPU reference implementation to validate.
- Check if any dynamic quantization steps affect stride calculations (int8 kernels vs fp16).

Next steps (short-term):
1) Add strict guard in selector (temporary): if (total_seq_len > kernel.max_seq_len) select next kernel OR assert loudly with full dump (we already have quick assert).
2) Add unit test to CI fuzz harness: generate prefix_len in [1800..4400], new_tokens in [4..2048], run selector logic + simulate pointer arithmetic to catch mismatch.
3) Run memory-corruption detector on repro image: run with cuda-memcheck + CUPTI tracing; collect kernel args (pointers, shapes) and dump in failing case to GH issue.
4) Trace build matrix: ensure cutlass builds we ship match runtime kernel metadata. Add small checksum of kernel metadata at startup to detect mismatches (could be a short-term telemetry).
5) Collaborate with platform infra to get determinism: pin allocator behavior by using jemalloc config to avoid reusing freed blocks in same addr ranges during reproducer runs.

Notes / breadcrumbs:
- Found earlier related scratchpad: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-20 (Ravi) - check his notes on rounding logic.
- PR 842 was an earlier attempt to change rounding heuristics; that PR introduced a subtle off-by-one in tile_count computation.

Proposed bug label / PR plan:
- Label: bug/kv-cache, severity: P1 (since causes crashes for long conversations), area: serving-runtime/attention
- Fix plan: 2-step: (A) hotfix selector to avoid selecting undersized kernel; (B) follow-up thorough audit of stride/pointer arithmetic + add CI fuzz tests.

Local quick commands I used (for myself):
- docker run --gpus all -v $(pwd):/work -w /work --rm serving-runtime:canary bash -c "pytest tests/repro/test_repl_seqlen_transition.py::test_repro_2048_to_3072 -q"
- ATTENTION_DEBUG=1 ATTN_FORCE_KERNEL=small_qk python repro/repro_seqlen_transition.py --log-level debug
- nvprof --profile-child-processes python repro/repro_seqlen_transition.py --profile

Anything else to try? (brain dump)
- Try reproducible run on AWS p4d (different driver/runtime) to rule out driver bug.
- Build a debug-only kernel binary with bounds checks (instrumented) and run reproducible workload to catch exact access index.
- Check for int vs size_t sign/overflow when computing offsets (e.g., int32 used for token index then multiplied by element stride -> overflow at ~2^31 is unlikely but watch types).

Open TODOs for next pairing session with Ravi/Sofia:
- [ ] Walk through kernel_selector.cpp and kv_buffer.cpp together (30m)
- [ ] Add failing-case artifact to PR (log + nvprof) (assign to Ravi)
- [ ] Draft hotfix PR that forces selection-safe kernel (me)
- [ ] Add fuzz-based unit test in CI (Sofia)

References / related docs:

- jira: ENG-1257 - "KV cache OOB when switching attention kernels at seqlen boundary"
- internal slack thread: #serving-runtime (ts=1694980000.000200)

-- end of scratchpad --
